### Problem Description
1. Model downloading fails or encounters connection issues without mirror failover and GGUF support in ModelDownloader.
2. Relying on external Ollama requires a heavy ~1.4GB host installation, modifies global state, and stores models in an isolated blob store that cannot be shared with the ComfyUI canvas.
3. Need an embedded, lightweight LLM runtime (llama-server from llama.cpp, ~19MB) with zero host pollution, standard OpenAI-compatible API, and shared GGUF models in engine/models/llm.

### Tasks
- [ ] Add GGUF format and mirror retry/failover to ModelDownloader and HubCatalog
- [ ] Enhance LlamaServerSupervisor with process supervision, auto-installation of standalone binary, and health checking
- [ ] Expose REST endpoints in main.py (/api/v1/llama-server/*) and manage lifecycle in FastAPI lifespan
- [ ] Connect LLMClient and AgentService to prioritize embedded llama_server
- [ ] Update SetupWizardModal.tsx and UI to manage embedded llama-server and download GGUF models directly
- [ ] Add unit tests and verify build
title: Feature: Embed llama-server (llama.cpp) and fix model downloading with universal GGUF sharing

### Description
In `frontend/src/components/canvas/WorkflowNode.tsx` (line 135), numeric inputs are parsed using `parseFloat(e.target.value)`. When a user clears the input box, `parseFloat("")` returns `NaN`.

### Impact
`NaN` values corrupt node parameter state and cause backend Pydantic validation errors during execution.

### Affected Files
- `frontend/src/components/canvas/WorkflowNode.tsx`

### Proposed Remediation
Guard against `NaN` with fallback defaults or schema minimums:
```typescript
const num = parseFloat(e.target.value);
updateParam(param.name, isNaN(num) ? param.default ?? 0 : num);
```
title: Bug: Unhandled NaN Parsing on Workflow Node Numeric Inputs

### Description
In `backend/app/runners/comfy_runner.py` (lines ~102, `poll_history_outputs`), the polling loop catches generic exceptions and only re-raises if `"ComfyUI execution error"` appears in the error message. Connection errors (like `httpx.ConnectError`) are logged at `DEBUG` and ignored.

If ComfyUI crashes, terminates, or refuses connections mid-generation, the runner continues polling in a silent loop for up to 120 seconds before timing out with a generic `TimeoutError`.

- `backend/app/runners/comfy_runner.py`

Detect consecutive connection failures or explicit HTTP error codes and fail fast rather than stalling for 2 minutes.

### Description
In `backend/app/core/cache.py` (lines ~75-115), asynchronous database methods (`get_async`, `set_async`, `clear_all_async`) wrap SQLite operations in bare `try...except Exception: pass`.

### Impact
If the SQLite database becomes locked, read-only, or corrupted, operations silently fail and degrade to in-memory caching without logging any warnings or errors.

### Affected Files
- `backend/app/core/cache.py`

### Proposed Remediation
Log database exceptions at `ERROR` level:
```python
except Exception as e:
    logger.error("Cache DB operation failed: %s", e)
```
title: Bug: Silent Exception Suppression in SQLite Cache Operations

body:
### Description
In `backend/app/runners/comfy_runner.py`, `backend/app/runners/api_runner.py`, and `backend/app/core/llm_client.py`, HTTP requests repeatedly open and close short-lived clients:
`async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=...) as client:`

During ComfyUI status polling (e.g. polling `/history` every 0.5s), a new TCP connection and SSL handshake occurs on every iteration.

### Impact
High request volume can cause socket exhaustion (accumulation of `TIME_WAIT` sockets), increased latency, and degraded system throughput.

### Affected Files
- `backend/app/runners/comfy_runner.py`
- `backend/app/runners/api_runner.py`
- `backend/app/core/llm_client.py`

### Proposed Remediation
Maintain long-lived `httpx.AsyncClient` instances tied to application/runner lifecycles with connection pooling enabled, and close them on shutdown.

labels.name: performance
labels.description: Performance, memory leaks, and socket/resource management

title: Performance: Socket Exhaustion Risk via Ephemeral `httpx.AsyncClient` Instances

Multiple state management stores and models rely heavily on `any` types:

- `frontend/src/stores/useCreativeStore.ts`
- `frontend/src/types/workflow.ts`

Define discriminated unions and typed parameter models representing the 5 core port data types (`string | image | audio | video | json`) and validate parameter payloads strongly in TypeScript.

body:
### Description
In `backend/app/runners/api_runner.py` (`_call_siliconflow_video`), the endpoint `/v1/video/submit` is handled as a synchronous response. The method immediately attempts to read `uri` or `url` directly from the submit response.

### Impact
SiliconFlow video generation is asynchronous; submitting a task returns a task/job ID, not the completed video URL. The current implementation returns incomplete payloads or fails, resulting in broken video links in the frontend.

### Affected Files
- `backend/app/runners/api_runner.py` (lines ~200+)

### Proposed Remediation
Implement an async polling mechanism similar to ComfyUI history checking:
1. Submit task and retrieve `job_id`.
2. Poll `/v1/video/status?job_id=...` with exponential backoff and timeout.
3. Return the final output URL once the status is `succeeded`.
title: Bug: SiliconFlow Video API Lacks Asynchronous Job Polling

body:
### Description
In `backend/app/main.py`, the workflow execution WebSocket endpoint does not explicitly catch `fastapi.WebSocketDisconnect`.

### Impact
When a client terminates or refreshes mid-execution, `await websocket.send_text(...)` raises a disconnect exception. The catch-all `except Exception as e:` catches this and attempts to send an error message back to the already-closed socket, triggering cascading socket exceptions in the backend logs.

### Affected Files
- `backend/app/main.py` (WebSocket execution route)

### Proposed Remediation
Explicitly catch `WebSocketDisconnect` and gracefully abort the execution loop:
```python
except WebSocketDisconnect:
    logger.info("Client disconnected from workflow run %s", run_id)
    # Perform node execution cleanup/cancellation without sending more socket frames
```
title: Bug: Unhandled WebSocketDisconnect Causes Cascading Errors in Execution Endpoint

body:
### Description
`ARCHITECTURE.md` and `AGENTS.md` (Invariant #5) require strict deterministic dirty-check caching. The specification mandates that canonical caching parameters include:
- Resolved seed
- Model identity/version
- Runner semantic version
- Provider identity (e.g. OpenAI vs. Fal.ai vs. SiliconFlow)

Currently, in `backend/app/core/cache.py` (`compute_semantic_node_hash`) and `backend/app/runners/creative_runner.py`, provider resolution occurs dynamically during execution but the resolved `provider_id` is never injected into `node.params`.

### Impact
Executing the same prompt across different providers (e.g. Fal.ai vs SiliconFlow) computes identical cache hashes. Switching providers yields false cache hits, returning previous generation outputs from a different provider.

### Affected Files
- `backend/app/core/cache.py`
- `backend/app/runners/creative_runner.py`
- `backend/app/runners/macro_compiler.py`

### Proposed Remediation
Inject provider identity and runner semantic version into hashing parameters:
```python
hash_params = {
    **clean_params,
    "__provider": provider_id,
    "__runner_ver": RUNNER_VERSION
}
```

labels.description: Critical priority issues that block core functionality or cause vulnerabilities

labels.name: architecture
labels.description: System architecture, contract invariants, and pipeline design

title: Bug: Deterministic Cache Hash Omits Provider Identity (Violates Invariant #5)

body:
### Description
In `backend/app/main.py`, the `CORSMiddleware` is configured with `allow_origins=["http://localhost:5173", "http://127.0.0.1:5173", "*"]` alongside `allow_credentials=True`.

### Impact
- Violates standard CORS specifications (browsers will reject or behave inconsistently with `*` when credentials are permitted).
- Severe security risk: enables potential Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) and unauthorized access where malicious third-party websites can make authenticated API requests against the user's local studio backend.

### Affected Files
- `backend/app/main.py` (lines ~126-132)

### Proposed Remediation
Remove `"*"` wildcard origin from `allow_origins`. Explicitly whitelist only localhost origins:
```python
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=[
        "http://localhost:5173",
        "http://127.0.0.1:5173",
    ],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)
```

labels.name: critical
labels.description: Critical priority issues that block core functionality or cause vulnerabilities

title: Security: Insecure CORS Configuration (Wildcard with Credentials)

## Problem Statement
When a generation task starts, the UI merely displays a generic spinning spinner and "Creating...". Because initial model loading can take several seconds and complex sampling takes time, users have no feedback on whether the system is stuck or actively processing.

## Proposed Changes
1. **Granular Execution Stages**:
   - Stream precise lifecycle phases from ComfyUI/Cloud runner via WebSocket events:
     - `Loading Model Checkpoint (e.g. 4.2GB)`
     - `Sampling Step X/Y (Percentage %)`
     - `Decoding Latent via VAE`
     - `Saving Asset to Store`
2. **Latent Denoising Preview**:
   - Stream intermediate latent images into the destination card placeholder during local generation, enabling creators to see their image emerge progressively from noise.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Users see human-readable, real-time stage updates during execution.
- [ ] Intermediate denoising steps render in the node placeholder when supported by the runner.
- [ ] Generation errors clearly highlight which stage encountered failure.

Clicking "Inpaint" currently launches a blocking, fullscreen modal (`InpaintModal`). This breaks the spatial immersion of the infinite canvas, prevents users from cross-referencing other assets on screen, and limits painting tools to a basic brush.

## Proposed Changes

- [ ] Mask data and coordinates remain strictly aligned with the source resolution upon submission.

## Problem Statement
The bottom creation dock currently displays parameters (Prompt, Aspect Ratio, Model selector, Seed) in a single static row. 
1. Newcomers are exposed to technical engine/model choices that can cause cognitive friction.
2. Advanced creators lack access to standard generation knobs (Negative Prompt, CFG Scale, Sampling Steps, LoRA weights).
3. When panning deep into the canvas, creators must constantly look back and forth between the focused image card and the fixed bottom dock.

## Proposed Changes
1. **Progressive Disclosure in Creation Dock**:
   - Default tier: Clean, minimal view focusing on Prompt, Aspect Ratio, and Variation Strength.
   - Advanced tier: Expandable popover/drawer exposing Negative Prompt, CFG Scale, Sampling Steps, and LoRA selectors.
2. **Contextual In-Place Floating Bubble**:
   - Float a lightweight action bar directly beneath the selected image card on the canvas with quick shortcuts (Vary, Inpaint, Upscale, Delete) to reduce mouse travel.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Primary dock remains compact and approachable by default.
- [ ] Advanced generation parameters can be toggled without cluttering the main canvas view.
- [ ] Selecting an image card brings up an inline action bubble adjacent to the card.

## Problem Statement
Currently, `ImageCardNode` elements appear scattered and isolated across the infinite canvas. While the backend records `provenance` metadata (parent image reference, seed, prompt changes), the user cannot visually discern how a design evolved from an initial concept into its current variation.

## Proposed Changes
1. **Ghost Lineage Edges**: When selecting an image card, render subtle, non-intrusive directional connection paths highlighting its parent source image and any derived child images.
2. **Auto-Branching Layout**: Add a one-click "Arrange Branch Tree" action to automatically format derivative variations into a structured gallery or tree hierarchy.

- [ ] Selecting an image card visually reveals its upstream parent and downstream variations.
- [ ] Deselecting cleanly hides the lineage paths to keep the canvas distraction-free.

## Epic Overview
Berry AI Studio has established a solid architectural foundation with its infinite canvas, selection-based creation dock, and hybrid cloud/local execution engine. To elevate the creative experience towards best-in-class generative workspaces (e.g., Figma, Leonardo AI, Midjourney Web), this tracking issue coordinates 6 focused UI/UX enhancements across the frontend canvas, docking system, inpainting tools, and agent interactions.

---

## Tracked Sub-Issues

- [ ] #33 — **[UX] Visual Lineage & Creative Branching Tree for Canvas Cards**
  *Ghost lineage paths upon selection and one-click variation tree/gallery arrangement.*
- [ ] #34 — **[UX] Progressive Disclosure & In-Place Floating Bubble in Creation Dock**
  *Dual-tier parameters (minimal default vs. advanced knobs) and inline action bubble near the active card.*
- [ ] #35 — **[UX] In-Place Canvas Inpainting & Expanded Masking Toolkit**
  *In-place canvas masking mode replacing the blocking fullscreen modal, with eraser and invert tools.*
- [ ] #36 — **[UX] Canvas Keyboard Shortcuts & Native Clipboard (Ctrl+V) Integration**
  *Direct image pasting at cursor coordinates, panning hand tool (`Space+Drag`), undo/redo history.*
- [ ] #37 — **[UX] Granular Generation Stages & Latent Denoising Previews**
  *Live execution phase breakdown via WebSocket and progressive latent image previews.*
- [ ] #38 — **[UX] Spatial Agent Collaboration & Canvas-Level Workspaces**
  *Canvas-level `/` shortcut trigger and auto-bounding multi-card concept workspaces.*

---

## Target Milestones & Deliverables
Each tracked issue can be picked up, implemented, and reviewed in standalone pull requests targeting `dev`.
